heading: LESSON OBJECTIVE
text: Calculate rectangle perimeter and solve missing-side or algebraic perimeter problems.

heading: CORE IDEA
text: Perimeter measures total distance around a shape, not the space inside it.

heading: KEY DEFINITIONS
text: Length and width are adjacent sides. Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal.

heading: CORE RULE
text: P=l+w+l+w=2(l+w). All side lengths must use the same unit.

heading: HOW IT WORKS
text: Add length and width, then multiply by two. For a missing side, use w=P/2−l.

heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 1
text: A 7 by 3 rectangle has P=2(7+3)=20 units.

heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 2
text: If P=30 and l=9, then w=30/2−9=6.

heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 3
text: A rectangle 4 cm by 25 mm is 4 cm by 2.5 cm. Its perimeter is 13 cm.

heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 4
text: If l=x+7, w=x+2 and P=54, solve 2(2x+9)=54 to get x=9.

heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 5
text: A 96 m perimeter needs 92 m of fencing if a 4 m gate replaces that portion.

heading: WHY THE RULE WORKS
text: A rectangle has two lengths and two widths, so l+w+l+w=2l+2w.

heading: VISUAL STRATEGY
text: Draw a rectangle, label opposite sides equally, and trace its outer boundary once.

heading: COMMON MISTAKES
text: Do not confuse area l×w with perimeter 2(l+w). Convert mixed units first.

heading: EXAM STRATEGY
text: Use P/2=l+w for missing dimensions. Subtract gates from fencing length, not from geometric perimeter.

heading: QUICK CHECK
text: If l=12,w=8 then P=40. If P=52,l=16 then w=10.

heading: RECAP AND NEXT STEP
text: P=2(l+w); use consistent units and count only exposed outer edges. Practice 18 problems, review answers, take the test.
